summary: Iteration 2 backend testing (driver + web-push + OSRM). 10/10 pytest cases PASSED against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Verified driver auth/role, /api/driver/pending 403 for regular user, OSRM estimate returns GeoJSON LineString (>2 coords) with 4 vehicle options, /api/trips/request stores OSRM geometry, full driver lifecycle (booking -> accept -> start -> arrive), auto-assign fallback after ~12s when no driver accepts, /api/driver/current, /api/driver/summary/today, VAPID public key (~87 chars base64url), push subscribe + push test (no crash with fake subscription).

minor.issue: Uses date-only string ('YYYY-MM-DD') compared with $gte against full ISO datetime strings stored in created_at. Works today but semantically comparing '2026-01-XX' < '2026-01-XXT..' lexicographically, could edge-fail at day boundaries.
Same date-string comparison as above; only counts trips whose status is arrived/completed/rated so 'trips completed today' filter is functional but based on created_at rather than completed_at.
History replay re-sends every prior user message on each call - will duplicate LLM turns and drive up cost/latency. Existing issue, not part of this iteration.

allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False - fine for Bearer header flow, but /api/auth/login sets an httpOnly cookie that will never be sent cross-origin from the SPA. Consider explicit origins + credentials=True if cookie auth is desired.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 894 lines - consider splitting (auth / trips / driver / push / ai) into modules for maintainability.

progress_trip uses asyncio.create_task without a task registry; on backend restart in-flight trips are stuck in 'searching'/'booking'. Consider persisting state and a worker that resumes/times-out pending trips.

AI chat history replay (server.py ~703-707) re-sends prior user messages sequentially to the LLM to 'keep memory consistent' - this scales O(n^2) in tokens and cost per session; use provider-native history or store/pass structured messages.

push subscription stored keyed by (user_id, endpoint) via update_one upsert - good. send_push_to_user properly deletes 410/404 subs, but silently swallows all other exceptions - consider structured logging.

Date filtering in /summary endpoints compares 'YYYY-MM-DD' with full ISO 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00' via $gte on strings; works but fragile. Store an explicit 'created_date' or use proper datetime type.

CORS allow_origins=['*'] with credentials=False is inconsistent with login setting an httpOnly SameSite=None cookie that will never be transmitted from a different origin - either keep header-only tokens (drop cookie) or switch to explicit origins + credentials.
